newsitem.title: FRANCE: Reuters French Advertising & Media Digest - May 21.
newsitem.headline: Reuters French Advertising & Media Digest - May 21.

text.p: REUTERS FRENCH ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST
News from Reuters and the French press on Advertising, Marketing, Media and Brand-name Products.
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:
PARIS - Ogilvy & Mather Paris aims to develop its role as a centre for coordinating the agency's internationally-managed budgets. (Le Figaro)
PARIS - Pillsbury Europe, owner of the Haagen-Dasz ice cream brand, has chosen Euro-RSCG to manage its European advertising, with a new campaign due before the end of this year. (Le Figaro)
PARIS - Publicis says its turnover rose six percent to 5.18 billion francs ($918.3 million) in the first quarter of 1997, largely due to expansion abroad. (Reuter)
MEDIA:
PARIS - The Conseil Superieur de l'Audiovisuel (CSA), the French broadcasting regulator, plans a tender for partial licenses to operate some 300 FM radio frequencies, its chairman says.
(Reuter)

PARIS - Mainstream French television channels, recently under fire for allegedly losing a million viewers, are seen by the public as politically biased, according to a poll carried out in the middle of the French election campaign. (Reuter)

PARIS - Turnover at publisher Filipacchi Medias rose to 375.1 million francs in the first quarter from 373.0 million in 1996's first three months, the company says. Magazine and advertising turnover fell in the period. (Reuter)
BRAND NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:
PARIS - French tobacco company Seita should post "satisfactory" operating profit this year despite losing market share to lower-priced products, Seita chairman Jean-Dominique Comolli says. (Reuter)

PARIS - LVMH Moet Hennessy Louis Vuitton says the failure of its DFS subsidiary to win the two principal concessions at Hong Kong's new airport would have only a "marginal" impact on DFS's business in Hong Kong. (Reuter)

PARIS - French carmaker Renault, complying with court rulings criticising the way it announced the closure of its plant in Vilvoorde, Belgium, will meet representativs of its European staff on June 3 to disccuss the shutdown. (Reuter)
Paris Editorial, Sue Landau
For further information and news, see Reuters Advertising & Media Briefing. And visit us on the Internet at http://www.Bizinfo.reuters.com
